name: Breath screening card
subtitle: a card that reads disease from a breath

effects.effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
crystals a few nanometres wide glow in a colour set purely by their size

effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
how: Tuberculosis and lung cancer are usually caught late because diagnosis needs a laboratory, and the illness announces itself in the breath months earlier. A card holds a grid of crystal sponges, each built to trap one of the telltale gases, and each pocket is seeded with size-tuned crystals whose glow is quenched as its gas fills the pores; a phone camera photographs the pattern of dimming and reads the breath like a colour chart.
obstacle: Breath differs with food, smoking, time of day and the mouth's own bacteria, so the pattern that means disease has to be learned over very large populations.
why: Puts a lab's gas chromatograph on a card a clinic can photograph.
real: The pieces exist separately - MOF film arrays read by a phone camera for VOCs, a MOF/quantum-dot fluorescent sensor for sub-ppb breath benzaldehyde, and porphyrin e-nose breath arrays field-tested for TB - but no integrated MOF+quantum-dot fluorescence card with phone readout was found.
